met:468764.summary: This tiny engraved gem, less than 2 cm high, is catalogued by the Metropolitan Museum as showing Christ before the elders; worn shapes of a larger draped figure and a smaller one can be made out in the translucent chalcedony. Intaglios like this were cut to be set in rings and used as seals, so that an owner could carry and impress a sacred image in daily life.
facts: The gem measures only about 1.9 × 1.6 cm and came to the Met in 1881 as a gift of John Taylor Johnston, the museum's first president.
Engraved gems (intaglios) were carved in reverse so that, pressed into wax or clay, they left a positive image; Christian subjects on gems appear from the 3rd–4th century onward.
met:468764.notes: The subject cannot be confirmed from the photographs: the engraving is worn and small, and the Met offers no published description. Identification rests on the Met's title alone. The scripture passage is uncertain ('elders' might mean the Sanhedrin, or the boy Jesus among the teachers, Luke 2:41–52), so none is given.
